messages:
kai (customer): Hey team — since last deploy ~08:45 UTC our requests are getting routed to eu-west even though client is in us-west, causing auth 401s and 400-600ms tail latency. Seen across multiple customers. Sample curl shows x-rw-region: us-west in request but response routed to eu-west.

emma (support): Sorry about that, can you paste a minimal curl + response headers? Also which API key/team is affected?

kai (customer): Here you go: 
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'x-rw-region: us-west' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response headers (snippet):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rw-region: eu-west
via: envoy/1.25.3
x-rw-fallback: regional-failover
content-length: 123
```
Body: latency ~520ms, and ~5% of requests returned 401 from auth.svc in eu-west.

emma (support): Thanks. Escalating to edge/runtime. @josh @sara can you take a look? Looks like header mismatch and fallback routing.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: config-change applied to /services/gateway/routes at 2025-11-04T08:40:12Z by infra@redwood (PR #4729).

josh (edge): I see related errors in the gateway logs. There is a timing window where the L7 route selector falls back if the affinity cookie isn't present and copies a region header from the chosen fallback cluster. That cluster has x-rw-region set to eu-west via override. Suspect header bleed when fallback path is used.

josh (edge): Repro: hit route with no session cookie + long tail -> route chooses fallback pool -> envoy header_mutation filter runs and sets x-rw-region based on cluster metadata.

sara (runtime): That would explain auth 401s — token validation is regional. If the request ends up in eu-west but token issued for us-west there are mismatches. Do we have an immediate mitigation?

josh (edge): Short-term: remove cluster-level x-rw-region header override or change header_mutation to set x-rw-origin (internal) instead of x-rw-region. Longer-term: switch routing to carry origin region in a preserved header and have auth service accept origin OR validate via token audience.

emma (support): Can we patch quickly? Customers are hitting billing + SLA impact. Also saw some retries leading to doubled token exchange charges.

josh (edge): I'll roll a hotfix to disable the override on the fallback cluster and add a conservative header filter to avoid overwriting incoming x-rw-region if present. Pushing in ~20m. Patch: 
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.header_mutation
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_mutation.v3.HeaderMutation
    response_headers_to_add:
      - header:
          key: x-rw-region
          value: "%DONT_OVERWRITE%"
```
(rough pseudo)

sara (runtime): I'll validate auth service tolerance once hotfix is live. Also flagging for a followup to add unit tests for fallback path so we don't regress.

kai (customer): Thanks — will monitor. Any ETA for rollback if this doesn't help?

josh (edge): Rollback plan ready; will revert the change and point traffic to previous pool within 5min if errors increase. I'll post an update once deployed.

emma (support): Thanks everyone. I'll keep the customer looped in. :thumbsup:

josh (edge): UPDATE: patch deployed at 1767770900. Early metrics show drop in cross-region hits from ~18% -> ~0.8% and 401s dropped to baseline. Continuing to monitor.

sara (runtime): Confirmed: auth error rate back to normal. Creating followup RFC for routing header hygiene and tests.

kai (customer): Verified on client side — latency back to normal (~35ms) and auth fixed. Thanks team! :tada:
